claims.statement: Retracts the lapse assertion in qclaim.living-doc-relapse.4abe5a8d177f. The rollout todo did not lapse: its review date was 2026-10-04 and it was re-read on 2026-10-03, and validate_living_docs.py reports a document stale only when its review_by date is earlier than the current date, so 2026-10-05 was the first day it would have reported stale. The accompanying consequence, that a lapse turns every open pull request red, is withdrawn with it.

correction.reason: The prior verified claim called a document re-read one day before its review date a lapse, and treated the review date itself as the day the check turns red. The validator fires on review_by earlier than today, so the first red day is the day after the review date, and nothing had gone unreviewed past it.
observations: scripts/validate_living_docs.py reports a document stale only when its review_by date is earlier than the current date, so a review date of 2026-10-04 first reports stale on 2026-10-05.

docs/todos/2026-09-20-living-document-rollout.md carried Review by 2026-10-04 and Reviewed 2026-10-03 when the retracted claim was made: re-read one day before the review date and two days before any red.
.github/workflows/governance-contracts.yml has no schedule trigger, so a lapse cannot turn an already completed check red; only a pull request whose checks run or re-run during the lapse fails.

The correction was previously prose inside the verified claim of qreceipt.post-merge-corrections.94ddb6f24550, where no validator or query could reach it. This receipt is that correction as the instrument the schema provides; the bytes of qreceipt.living-doc-relapse.4abe5a8d177f are deliberately unchanged, because a receipt records what was believed at its subject commit.
